q8.answer: Counts live in one shared Redis (primary with replica) under the key rl:{customerId}:{windowNumber}, where windowNumber is Redis time in seconds divided by 60, rounded down. Each key is given an expiry about 60 seconds after its window ends, so old counts clean themselves up.

q9.answer: The budget resets when the clock minute rolls over. Each fixed window has its own key, and a new window starts at count 0. There is no other recovery mechanism, and a 429 does not consume budget.

q10.answer: The check and increment run as one Lua script on Redis, which executes atomically with no other command in between. If the count is at or above the limit, the script returns denied and changes nothing. Otherwise it increments, so two gateways cannot both admit the last slot.

q11.answer: Retry-After is max(1, 60 - (now mod 60)) in whole seconds, where now is Redis time in seconds. That is the time until the current fixed window ends and the budget resets.

q12.answer: I did not decide any retry. The design makes one call with a 50 ms timeout, and on error or timeout it forwards the request, emits ratelimit_store_unavailable, and ignores any late reply. The client gets the normal backend response with no X-RateLimit-Limit or X-RateLimit-Remaining headers, because the count is unknown.
